# Method notes: #4766

Observations from triaging this single issue. Not applied to `SKILL.md` or `scripts/` — per
the per-issue worker boundary, only recorded here for collation to consider.

## Compiler-registry provenance note is stale, but the field that matters is not

`.cache/compilers/main-debug.json` (shared cache, not touched by this session) carries a
`provenance_note` field that still names the *previous* batch's public commit
(`13730886e`, with `built_at` predating this session) even though the top-level `git_commit`
field was already updated to this batch's ground truth,
`89e2f98e29c289ae8ad9e00dd310104fea9fd7df`. The `version` field (self-reported `7665270b9`)
matches `dxc --version` run directly against the registered executable, and `git_commit` is
the field `run`/capture headers should consult, so this did not affect any measurement for
this issue — but the free-text `provenance_note` disagreeing with `git_commit` in the same
JSON file is confusing for the next reader and worth `triage.py compiler` re-stamping it
consistently on registration (or dropping the prose field in favour of only the structured
one) at collation, rather than a per-issue worker editing shared cache state.

## A build-configuration ask needs the provenance control even with zero compile involved

This issue has no shader and is `not-compiler-verifiable`, so none of the run/bisect machinery
applies — but the ground-truth provenance check (`git diff --name-only <build-sha>
<upstream-sha>`, with the older-ancestor control) is still exactly as load-bearing here as on a
crash issue: the whole verdict rests on "the CMakeLists.txt line at ground truth reads X", and
without the equivalence check that citation is just as unverifiable as an uncontrolled crash
predicate would be. Recorded as `manual-case-cmake-history.txt`, generated by a small script
(`capture-cmake-history.py`) rather than transcribed, per the existing rule for
`manual-case-*.txt` captures — this generalises that rule to a source-reading probe that never
touches `dxc.exe` at all.

## `check_paths.py` currently fails, but not because of this issue

At the time of this triage, `python scripts/check_paths.py` reports machine-path leaks in
`data/issues/4786/`, `data/issues/4858/`, `data/issues/4888/` and `data/issues/4958/` — none of
which is this issue's directory, and none was touched here (out of the strict per-issue
boundary). This issue's own new files (`capture-cmake-history.py`,
`manual-case-cmake-history.txt`) were checked individually and are clean (no `4766` line appears
in the gate's failure output). Flagging for collation since a batch-wide `check_paths.py` run
will currently fail regardless of this issue's own cleanliness.

## A related, still-open issue can be the strongest evidence for a build-question issue

Issue #5985 discusses #4766 explicitly (a contributor cites it by number while explaining why a
DllMain refactor would enable static linking), and a maintainer's most recent comment there
(2024-10-28, no reply since) asks the exact question this issue is about. That is stronger,
dated evidence of "still open, still unaddressed" than re-stating the CMake facts alone would
be, and it was found only by reading the cross-reference timeline during step 1 as instructed —
worth flagging because for a `question`/`build`-labelled issue with no shader, the timeline read
is doing most of the evidentiary work that `bisect` would do for a crash.
